## Problem

A vLLM server answers the OpenAI-compatible protocol — `/v1/models`,
`/v1/completions`, `/v1/chat/completions` — on port 8000. The
operator's instinct is that `--api-key` secures it. Upstream documents
otherwise: the key guards ONLY the `/v1`, `/v2`, `/inference`,
`/cohere` path prefixes. Utility and control endpoints on the same
server authenticate NOTHING even with the key set. The class:
`/metrics`, `/load`, `/invocations`, `/pause`,
`/abort_requests`, `/update_weights`. A server believed keyed still
runs an unauthenticated inference route (`/invocations`). It also
exposes its Prometheus telemetry to anyone on the segment. vLLM's own
security page says so in one line worth quoting verbatim: "Do not rely
exclusively on
`--api-key` for securing access to vLLM. Additional security measures
are required for production deployments." The manifest maps the
surface to OWASP LLM02 + LLM10. The ATLAS mapping is AML.T0049 +
T0050 (the pre-#210 paired attack row carried it; phantom-upstream,
removed — os#210; the matrix is published). The task: the key-on
probe pair splits the two classes — guarded vs unauthenticated on the
same port. Then flip the posture and watch both close.

## Solution

Serve the lab target. Set the key. Run BOTH classes of probe. The
pair's point: the classes behave differently on one port:

```bash
# 1. BOOT THE LAB TARGET in the keyed-and-exposed posture:
#      vllm serve <model> --api-key <sk-lab-key> --host 0.0.0.0
#    (uvicorn's host default is 127.0.0.1 — an explicit broad bind is
#     the deliberate lab act; run it in an isolated lab segment, and
#     see [Gate lab-mode and exp-classified tools]
#    (../admin/lab-mode-gating.html) for how exp A-7 rows reach a lab
#     host — this recipe drives the shapes with curl, base system)
#
# 2. KEYED CLASS — /v1/* rejects the keyless request, honours it:
curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' http://<target>:8000/v1/models
#    -> 401  (Bearer key required on the /v1 prefix)
curl -s -H 'Authorization: Bearer <sk-lab-key>' http://<target>:8000/v1/models
#    -> {"object":"list","data":[{"id":"<model>", ...}]}
curl -s -H 'Authorization: Bearer <sk-lab-key>' \
     http://<target>:8000/v1/completions \
     -d '{"model":"<model>","prompt":"Reply OK only.","max_tokens":4}'
#    -> {"id":"cmpl-...","choices":[{"text":"OK", ...}]}

# 3. UNGUARDED CLASS — SAME server, SAME port, key SET, no Bearer sent:
curl -fsS http://<target>:8000/metrics | head
#    -> Prometheus exposition (request latencies, token counts, queue) —
#       no 401; vLLM's docs list /metrics among endpoints needing NO key
curl -fsS http://<target>:8000/load
#    -> server-load surfaces, no key required
curl -s http://<target>:8000/tokens -o /dev/null; echo
#    utility route class: the /v1 gate does not cover it (probe the
#    shape you care about; /tokenize-class routes answer without 401)
#    /invocations routes to the SAME inference functions as /v1 —
#    unauthenticated inference on the same port, the strongest probe.
#    Control verbs (/pause, /abort_requests, /update_weights) are
#    unauthenticated per upstream's unprotected list — treat their
#    shapes as read-only reconnaissance unless your lab authorises the
#    state change; the PROBE evidence does not need them fired.
```

Then the verification leg — flip the posture, re-run BOTH classes:

```bash
# 4. THE FLIP: loopback bind (module posture) — the segment loses the
#    whole port, guarded and unguarded alike; with it up, a firewall
#    policy in front of vLLM is the load-bearing control, because the
#    key never covered the unguarded class:
sudo nixos-rebuild test     # lab configuration: loopback-only serve

# 5. SAME probes, same box:
curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' http://<target>:8000/metrics
#    -> FAIL (refused) from the segment — /metrics no longer reachable
curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' \
     -H 'Authorization: Bearer <sk-lab-key>' http://<target>:8000/v1/models
#    -> FAIL (refused) — the keyed class closed with it. Diff = evidence.
```

Expected output shape (abridged, shapes not transcripts):

```
sweep @ http://<target>:8000  posture: --api-key set, bind 0.0.0.0
  /v1/models  (no key)     -> 401        # guard holds on /v1
  /v1/models  (Bearer)     -> ok {"object":"list",...}
  /v1/completions (Bearer) -> ok {"id":"cmpl-...",...}
  /metrics    (no key)     -> 200 PROMETHEUS EXPOSITION  # unguarded
  /load       (no key)     -> 200                        # unguarded
  /invocations(no key)     -> inference without 401      # unguarded
sweep again, posture: loopback-only
  all probes -> FAIL (refused) — both classes closed to the segment
```

## Discussion

- **Why plain curl and not a bespoke exploit script:** the paired
  attack manifest row was a PHANTOM. Its claimed kailash-os
  upstream was never created. The os#210 audit removed it
  (2026-10-14; https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/issues/210 —
  the name rides the registry). The probe leg runs the protocol
  directly with the base system only — nothing invented. A real A-7
  tool re-enters via the os#210 rebuild contract, installing only via
  the double-key lab gate (walk:
  [Gate lab-mode and exp-classified
  tools](../admin/lab-mode-gating.html)).
- **The verbatim caveat is the recipe's thesis.** vLLM's security
  page states the key guards only the `/v1`, `/v2`, `/inference`,
  `/cohere` path prefixes. It then adds the verbatim warning:
  "Do not rely exclusively on
  `--api-key` for securing access to vLLM. Additional security
  measures are required for production deployments." Upstream's
  recommendation for anything others can reach: a reverse proxy (or
  firewall) that allows only the intended routes. That is why the
  defence leg is a network policy. The key was never the whole answer
  for the unguarded class, and no vLLM flag makes it one.
- **/metrics is the sleeper finding:** every published scrape target
  is an unauthenticated read of token counts, latencies and error
  rates. It gives request-pattern inference about the tenants; no key
  is ever checked. Gate it at the proxy/firewall like the unguarded
  inference route. An exporter that runs on the machine itself keeps
  the port closed to the segment.
- **Bind discipline is the second control:** uvicorn defaults to
  127.0.0.1:8000. An explicit `--host 0.0.0.0` is a deliberate act
  and a lab-segment one. The posture flip here is coarse on purpose —
  it closes everything at once, so the diff is unambiguous.
  Production vLLM wants bind discipline PLUS a proxy allowlist on the
  prefixes the deployment intends to keep public.
- **The observability defence leg is a pending row, stated honestly:**
  Langfuse is the trace destination the manifest owns for LLM
  request/answer telemetry. The app can emit via self-hosted
  docker-compose, or via the OTel endpoint `/api/public/otel`. The
  export carries `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS` with
  `Basic <pk-lf-…>:<sk-lf-…>`, plus the
  `x-langfuse-ingestion-version: 4` header. Per-request cost/latency
  tracing lands next to the probe findings (the
  kailash-langfuse module row is pending/unwired at the pin, PENDING
  — the upstream export shape above is quoted as the design). Traces
  give the anomaly view the probes hand-verified: requests that
  bypassed expectation, token counts that never reconcile.
- **This is the transferable pattern:** lab target up → keyed +
  keyless probes against one port → posture flip → same probes →
  diff. Origin walk with the verdict instrument:
  [Attack the platform, then verify](attack-then-verify.html).
